records.summary: Flanking: Flanking is when two or more characters surround a single opponent, giving them advantage on their attacks. Use this tactic to overwhelm tough opponents or take down enemies quickly. Cover: Use cover to your advantage by hiding behind objects or structures to avoid taking damage from ranged attacks. Be aware that enemies can also use cover against you, so try to move around to get a better angle on them. Crowd Control: Crowd control spells and abilities can be used to temporarily incapacitate enemies, giving you time to focus on other targets or to retreat. Examples include spells that inflict conditions

To escape from restraints like ropes, chains, or bindings, you generally attempt a Strength or Dexterity check (whichever the GM deems appropriate) or use a suitable tool or ability to assist in your escape. You may have to make a check against the restraints' Strength check or a predetermined difficulty set by the DM. Abilities or spells may also aid in escaping restraints.

Benefit: Grants bonuses to scavenging checks and occasionally provides extra items without checks. Level 1 (Basic): +1 bonus to scavenging checks, 1 extra item per expedition without a check. Level 2 (Advanced): +2 bonus to scavenging checks, 2 extra items per expedition without a check. Level 3 (Expert): +3 bonus to scavenging checks, 3 extra items per expedition without a check.

Dice Rolls: For a chase, each participant rolls a D20, adding modifiers based on their freerunning skills, dexterity, and any environmental advantages. Obstacle Difficulty: Obstacles have varying difficulties (DCs) based on complexity. For instance, a simple fence might have a DC 10, while a wall with narrow ledges could have a DC 15. Obstacles can have their Dc's adjusted by the GM to reflect certain obstacles being more difficult or easier.

Different freerunning moves can bypass obstacles with varying proficiency. Here are a few examples: 1. Vault: A basic move involving clearing obstacles by jumping over them. This can include hurdles, fences, or low walls. It emphasizes swift clearance and efficiency. (DC 10): Roll a D20 + Dexterity modifier. Succeeds on a roll of 10 or higher. Higher rolls may indicate faster or more stylish vaults. 2. Wall Run: Running up a vertical surface, using momentum to gain height or reach ledges that might be out of immediate reach. It requires strong leg power and precise foot placement.* (DC 15): Roll a D20 + Strength or Dexterity modifier (player's choice). Succeeds on a roll of 15 or higher. Higher rolls might allow for reaching greater heights or distances. 3. Precision Jump: A precise leap from one point to another, often over gaps or onto narrow surfaces. This move demands accuracy, balance, and spatial awareness. (DC 12-18): Roll a D20 + Dexterity modifier. Difficulty varies based on the gap's size or narrowness of the surface. Typically, a roll of 12 to 18 is needed for success, with larger gaps requiring higher rolls. 4. Climb-Up: Pulling oneself up and over an obstacle, such as a wall or ledge. This move involves upper body strength and agility. (DC 10-15): Roll a D20 + Strength or Dexterity modifier. The difficulty depends on the height or complexity of the obstacle. Succeeds on a roll of 10 to 15. 5. Cat Leap: Jumping from one wall to another, often horizontally, and using hands to grasp and pull oneself up onto the second wall. It requires coordination and upper body strength. (DC 15): Roll a D20 + Dexterity modifier. Succeeds on a roll of 15 or higher due to the complexity of the maneuver and reliance on upper body strength. 6. Underbar: Passing underneath an obstacle, like a railing or a bar, while maintaining momentum. This move requires flexibility and speed. (DC 12): Roll a D20 + Dexterity modifier. Succeeds on a roll of 12 or higher, as it requires speed, flexibility, and timing. 7. Lache: Swinging from one object to another using momentum, often seen when moving between bars or structures. It combines swinging, timing, and grip strength. (DC 15): Roll a D20 + Strength or
If the Underbar fails, the character loses momentum and struggles to pass under the obstacle, reducing their movement speed by an additional 5 feet for that round.
If the check fails, the character stumbles or struggles with the obstacle, losing the chance to clear it efficiently. The character's movement speed is reduced by an additional 5 feet for that round.

Environmental hazards leverage nature's dangers, adding realism and risk to outdoor encounters. - Quicksand: Targets who fail a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check each round begin to sink, reducing their movement speed by half. If they sink completely, they are restrained and must succeed on a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check to escape or be rescued. - Freezing Water: Each minute of exposure, targets must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution save or take 1 level of exhaustion and have their movement speed halved. Prolonged exposure (5 minutes) forces a DC 15 Constitution save or suffer 1d6 cold damage per minute. - Avalanche: Targets in the avalanche path make a DC 14 Dexterity save or take 4d6 bludgeoning damage and are buried. Buried targets can attempt a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check each round to dig free. - Poisonous Spores: A DC 13 Constitution save is required to avoid poisoning from inhaling spores. Failure causes the poisoned condition for 1d4 hours. Each round of exposure requires another save. - Swarming Insects: Players in a 15-ft radius of the swarm must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity save each turn or take 1d4 piercing damage. Players who fail three saves are also poisoned for 1 hour. Burning Embers: Small embers or coals cover the ground. Moving through them requires a DC 13 Dexterity save each round, or the player takes 1d6 fire damage. Embers can reignite if disturbed, creating additional hazards. Razorvine: Dense patches of razor-sharp foliage that can cut through clothing. Moving through it requires a DC 14 Dexterity save each round; failure results in 2d4 slashing damage. Fumaroles: Steam vents that erupt unpredictably, dealing 1d8 fire damage to anyone within 10 feet. Players must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save to avoid burns. Awareness of these vents requires a

In high-fantasy settings, magic-infused hazards can provide unique, unpredictable challenges. - Cursed Ground: Every turn spent on cursed ground requires a DC 14 Constitution save. Failure results in 1d6 necrotic damage, while success causes mild discomfort. Those who fail three saves in a row are cursed, taking disadvantage on further saves. - Mana Storm: In a mana storm, players make a DC 15 Wisdom save each round or are subjected to random magical effects (e.g., 1d6 wild magic surges or temporary polymorphs). - Mirror Surfaces: Mirror illusions require a DC 13 Intelligence save to recognize. Players who fail are affected by a reflection spell (e.g., trapped or dazed) until they succeed on the save.

Natural disasters introduce high-stakes, large-scale threats that drive urgency and tension. - Earthquakes: Tremors force a DC 14 Dexterity save each round to avoid falling prone. Structures may collapse on a failed DC 15 Constitution save, potentially trapping players. - Tornadoes or Sandstorms: In sandstorms, a DC 12 Constitution save is needed every minute to avoid exhaustion. Tornadoes require a DC 16 Strength save each round to remain grounded. Failure may fling players 10 feet in a random direction. - Lava Flow: Players near lava must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save each round or take 2d6 fire damage from intense heat. Crossing lava flows without flight or magical protection requires a DC 17 Dexterity save, or they take 6d6 fire damage. - Flooding: Rising waters impose difficult terrain. Players must succeed on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check each minute to avoid being pulled under, and a DC 12 Constitution save every 10 minutes to avoid

Structural hazards capitalize on the dangers of decayed or trap-laden structures. - Falling Ceilings: A sudden collapse deals 3d8 bludgeoning damage to all in a 10-ft radius. A DC 15 Dexterity save avoids the damage, and players can use DC 13 Wisdom (Perception) to notice weakened ceiling sections in advance. - Collapsing Bridge: The bridge begins to crumble, requiring a DC 14 Dexterity save to cross safely. Failure causes a fall or necessitates climbing (DC 15 Strength check) to pull back up. - Swinging Blades: Blades require a DC 13 Dexterity save each time they pass. Players may attempt a DC 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) to disable the mechanism. - Crumbling Floor: If players step on weakened tiles, they must succeed on a DC 12 Dexterity save to avoid falling through and taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage. - Spiked Pits: Hidden pits require a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to jump over, or a DC 14 Perception check to spot in time. Falling in deals 2d10 piercing damage, and escaping requires a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. Collapsing Wall: Triggered by loud sounds or impact, a wall falls, forcing players within 15 feet to make a DC 14 Dexterity save or take 3d6 bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone.

In sci-fi or tech-heavy fantasy settings, technological hazards create unique threats. - Laser Grids: Motion-activated, these grids deal 3d6 slashing damage to anyone passing through. Disarming the grid requires a DC 16 Intelligence (Engineering) check or DC 18 Dexterity (Sleight of

Elixirs are powerful concoctions created through advanced alchemy to target specific ailments or conditions, from poisons to curses. - Elixir of Detoxification: Neutralizes most poisons and removes toxins from the bloodstream. Restores 1d6 HP per hour for 3 hours and grants immunity to the same toxin for 24 hours. Requires a Resilience Check (DC 10 + toxin potency) to avoid mild dizziness. - Anticurse Elixir: Temporarily suspends the effects of a curse for 12 hours. Requires a Crafting Check (DC 15) and an optional Occultism Check (DC 12) to extend duration. If consumed more than once in 24 hours, the character suffers -1 penalty to Willpower until they rest. - Revitalizing Brew: Speeds up recovery by granting +1 HP per hour for the next 24 hours. If consumed more than twice in a week, it causes nervous exhaustion, imposing a -2 penalty to Focus until the character abstains. - Elixir of Fortitude: Grants 5 temporary HP for 4 hours and a +2 bonus to Resilience Checks against fear effects. Overuse within 24 hours causes the character to suffer -1 penalty to Insight as their resilience drops after the boost. - Overuse and Side Effects: After consuming more than two elixirs in one day, characters make a Resilience Check (DC 12 + elixir potency) or suffer mild toxicity effects (e.g., dizziness or mild hallucinations) for 8 hours. ---

Ancestral Blessing is a ritual wherein the healer calls upon the spirits of ancestors or revered elders to bestow protective and healing energies. - Healing Effect: The healer calls on ancestral spirits, making a Spiritual Check (DC 16). Success restores 3d8 HP and grants a +2 bonus to Resilience Checks for 24 hours. - Protective Spirits: As part of the ritual, the ancestral spirits grant the target protection, reducing all physical damage by 1d4 for 24 hours. - Ancestral Guidance: On a critical success, the target receives a vision or symbolic message from the ancestors, potentially revealing helpful guidance, hints, or insight for their current path. - Ancestorʼs Wrath: Failure on the Spiritual Check risks drawing ancestral disfavor. The healer or target must succeed on a Willpower Check (DC 14) to avoid a minor curse, such as a temporary -1 penalty to Strength or Insight for 24 hours. ---

Psionic healers can cleanse harmful energies, such as curses, toxins, or psychic residue, and realign the characterʼs energy to support holistic recovery. - Aura Cleanse: The healer can purify the targetʼs aura, removing psychic toxins, curses, or disruptive energy. This requires a Psionic Check (DC 15) and removes one minor curse, poison, or psychic affliction. - Advanced Cleansing: By increasing the DC to 18, the healer can remove complex curses or long- term ailments. Failure risks contamination, causing the healer to suffer a -1 penalty to Resilience for 24 hours. - Energy Realignment: Using mental focus, the healer realigns the characterʼs energy to promote balance and recovery. This grants the target a +2 bonus to recovery-related rolls (such as Rest or Resilience Checks) for the next 24 hours. - Psychic Shielding: The healer establishes a protective psychic barrier around the target, preventing new afflictions or curses from taking effect for 24 hours. This requires a Psionic Check (DC 17). Failure imposes mental strain, causing the healer to suffer -1 to Focus until they complete a long rest. ---

Advanced bioengineering devices and synthetic agents that allow regrowth of tissues, bones, and even organs. - Synth-Bone Injector: A specially engineered injection that stimulates bone regeneration, ideal for fractures and breaks. Restores 2d6 HP and heals minor fractures over 12 hours. Limited to once every 48 hours, with side effects if overused (-1 to Strength for 24 hours). - Organ Regenerator: For serious internal injuries, this device stimulates the regrowth of damaged organs. Requires a Bioengineering Check (DC 18) and heals 6d6 HP over 24 hours. After use, characters feel weak, suffering a -1 penalty to Constitution for 48 hours. - Synthetic Skin Patch: These bioengineered patches bond to damaged skin, providing rapid healing for burns or abrasions. Restores 2d6 HP and grants immunity to infection for 24 hours. Limited to two uses per week. - Stem Cell Injector: Injects lab-grown stem cells to accelerate the bodyʼs natural healing processes. Requires a Medical Check (DC 16), restoring 4d6 HP over 8 hours. Each use in the same week increases the DC by 2 due to risk of rejection. ---

Celestial Touch is one of the most potent mystical healing techniques, involving the channelling of divine or celestial energy to fully restore a characterʼs health and remove all afflictions. - Healing Effect: Once per week, a healer who channels celestial or divine energy can use this ability to fully restore a characterʼs HP and cure all ailments, including curses, poisons, and psychic damage. - Spiritual Check and Ritual: The ritual takes one hour, requiring a Spiritual Check (DC 20). Success restores all HP and grants immunity to fear and mental ailments for 48 hours. - Radiant Aura: After the ritual, the target gains a radiant glow for 24 hours, attracting spiritual or planar beings sensitive to divine energy. While this glow may be harmless, it can potentially draw both benevolent and curious spirits or even planar entities. - Divine Exhaustion: If used more than once a week, the healer risks divine exhaustion. Each additional use requires a Resilience Check (DC 18) by the healer. Failure results in -1 penalty to their magical abilities or spells for 72 hours due to spiritual depletion. - Celestial Bond: Occasionally, the target forms a temporary “bond” with a celestial being who aided in the ritual. This bond provides guidance or a small blessing (e.g., +1 to Insight for 48 hours), but may occasionally ask for favors or observances in return. ---

These modules are specialized for characters with cybernetic or synthetic enhancements, capable of healing both biological and mechanical injuries. - Standard Cyber Repair Module: Restores 2d8 HP to both biological and synthetic parts. Requires an Engineering Check (DC 12) for effective repair and prevents infection in both organic and synthetic wounds. - Advanced Cyber Repair Unit: An enhanced version capable of restoring 4d8 HP and recalibrating cybernetic parts for optimal function. Requires an Engineering Check (DC 15) and grants a temporary +1 bonus to Dexterity for 4 hours. - Synthetic Fiber Rejuvenator: Used for repairing synthetic skin, artificial muscles, and biofiber components. Restores 2d6 HP specifically to synthetic tissues and requires an Engineering Check (DC 12). Failure risks fiber malfunction (-1 penalty to Strength) until repaired. - Self-Repair Module: A high-tech implant that allows cybernetic components to self-repair minor damage over time. Grants 1 HP regeneration per hour for 12 hours. Limited to once per day, with overuse risking overheating of synthetic parts (-1 to Dexterity for 24 hours).

Divine Intervention is a last-resort ritual that invokes direct assistance from a god, celestial, or other higher power to provide complete healing and intervention against severe afflictions. - Effect: With a Spiritual Check (DC 22), the healer invokes a higher being to restore the target to full health, remove all afflictions, and grant divine protection (resistance to all damage types) for 24 hours. - Cost and Conditions: This powerful ritual can only be performed once per month and may carry divine obligations, such as offering sacrifices, performing ceremonies, or acting on the deityʼs behalf. - Potential Divine Favor: Upon success, thereʼs a 25% chance the deity may grant a lasting blessing (e.g., +1 to Willpower or Resilience) until the target performs a task aligned with the deityʼs will. - Divine Repercussions: Failure or misuse of Divine Intervention risks invoking wrath. The target must make a Willpower Check (DC 18) to avoid receiving a minor divine curse, such as temporary bad luck (-1 to all d20 rolls for 48 hours). ---

- Cleansing Stone: An artifact worn as a pendant, releasing waves of calming energy. Grants a permanent +1 bonus to Willpower but risks curse effects if cravings are ignored for too long. - Serenity Crystal: A rare artifact that emits a soothing aura, reducing withdrawal symptoms by one level. After seven uses, however, the crystal may shatter or cause unpredictable side effects, such as a temporary -2 penalty to Focus for 24 hours. - Side Effects of Magic Use: Magic is potent but taxing. Characters relying heavily on spells or artifacts for recovery may develop a dependency on these tools, facing increased cravings without them. - Curse Risk: Overuse of magical assistance may lead to a curse effect. After using a Serenity Crystal or similar artifact for seven consecutive days, characters roll a Luck Check (DC 10); on a failure, they gain a minor curse, such as a -1 penalty to Willpower in certain realms or vulnerabilities to psionic attacks.

Ethereal Channeling allows a healer to draw energy from the ethereal plane to mend wounds and protect against spirit-based attacks. - Healing Effect: The healer performs a Spiritual Check (DC 18) to successfully channel ethereal energy, healing 4d6 HP and granting the target resistance to spirit-based attacks (e.g., wraiths, ghosts) for 12 hours. - Ethereal Empowerment: By increasing the DC to 20, the healer can grant an additional 1d4 temporary HP that absorbs spiritual damage for 24 hours. - Risk of Etheric Imbalance: More than two channelings in a week risk etheric imbalance, causing the target to become partially attuned to the ethereal plane. The target must succeed on a Resilience Check (DC 15) to avoid suffering from ethereal “bleed,” which appears as ghostly hallucinations or echoes (-1 to Focus for 24 hours).

- Ritual Effects: Ethereal rituals are mystical ceremonies that can momentarily weaken addictionʼs hold. These are usually performed by shamans, mystics, or priests with proficiency in ritualistic magic. - Purification Ritual: A one-hour ceremony that involves incense, chanting, and the infusion of positive energies. Grants a +2 bonus to Resilience Checks against cravings and withdrawal for 48 hours. - Spirit Shield: This protective ritual grants the character immunity to cravings for one day but comes with a risk of temporary spiritual fatigue, as described below. - Energy Cost and Side Effects: Rituals take a toll on the characterʼs spirit. After a Spirit Shield ritual, characters must succeed on a Resilience Check (DC 12) or suffer -1 to Focus until they rest. Frequent use (more than once per week) increases the Resilience Check to DC 15. ---

- Herb Effects: Different herbs have various effects that ease specific symptoms, reduce cravings, or grant temporary mental fortification. - Calma Leaf: Reduces mental strain, granting a +1 bonus to all Willpower Checks against cravings for 8 hours. - Tranquil Root: Temporarily suppresses physical withdrawal symptoms, reducing penalties by one stage for 4 hours. - Mindflower: Clears the mind, reducing confusion and mental fog, and granting a +1 bonus to Focus and Insight checks for 4 hours. - Preparation and Use: Characters can prepare herbal mixtures using a Herbalism or Medicine Check (DC 12). Failure wastes the herb. Successfully prepared herbs can be consumed as needed. - Side Effects: Overuse of herbs may result in tolerance, requiring a higher dosage or causing minor side effects, such as fatigue. After using any herb three times in a week, characters roll a Resilience Check (DC 10); on a failure, the herbʼs effects are reduced by half until the character abstains for one week.

Herbal remedies are commonly used for minor injuries and to ease discomfort. Different herbs have specific effects, and skilled characters can combine these to enhance recovery. - Calma Leaf: A soothing herb that reduces inflammation. Restores 1d6 HP and grants a +1 bonus to Resilience Checks against pain-based effects for 4 hours. Multiple doses in one day require a Herbalism Check (DC 12) to avoid nausea. - Tranquil Root: A potent herb that calms the nerves. Restores 1d6 HP and reduces penalties from shock or trauma by one level for 4 hours.

Alchemists create healing potions of various strengths, each with unique brewing requirements and cooldowns to avoid dependency or toxicity. - Minor Healing Potion: Restores 2d4 HP instantly. Basic recipe with moderate availability. Cooldown of 1 hour before another healing potion can be consumed. - Standard Healing Potion: Restores 4d4 HP. Requires a Crafting Check (DC 12) to brew. Cooldown of 3 hours. - Major Healing Potion: Restores 6d4 HP. Requires a Crafting Check (DC 15). Cooldown of 8 hours to avoid strain on the body. - Superior Healing Elixir: Restores 8d4 HP, but carries risks. Requires a Crafting Check (DC 18) to successfully brew, and drinking it imposes a Resilience Check (DC 14) to avoid side effects (e.g., temporary -2 penalty to Constitution for 24 hours). - Cooldown and Dependency: Repeated use of potions without cooldown leads to diminishing returns, reducing healing by 1d4 HP per potion after the first and imposing -1 penalty to Resilience until the

Nature-based remedies, alchemy, and potions are common across various multiversal settings. - Healing Herbs and Poultices: Herbs such as Calma Leaf or Tranquil Root restore 1d6 HP and reduce inflammation when applied directly. Multiple applications require a Herbalism Check (DC 12) to avoid overdose effects (e.g., nausea). - Healing Potions: Basic healing potions restore 2d4 HP; stronger concoctions restore 4d4, 6d4, or more. Brewing potions requires a Crafting Check (DC varies by potion strength), and each potion has a cooldown before another can be consumed. - Alchemical Elixirs: Created through alchemy, elixirs can accelerate recovery or cure specific ailments (e.g., poison or curse effects). Characters must succeed on a Resilience Check (DC 10 + potion potency) to avoid side effects, such as dizziness or mild toxicity.

- Skilled herbalists can combine up to three herbs in a single poultice to amplify effects, requiring a Herbalism Check (DC 15). Success grants enhanced effects (e.g., additional 1d4 HP or extended duration), while failure results in toxicity (e.g., -1 penalty to Resilience for 24 hours). - Combining herbs with opposing properties (e.g., stimulating and calming) automatically imposes a -1 penalty to Focus. ---

Portable, field-grade devices designed to prevent death in critical situations by stabilizing a characterʼs life force. - Basic Life Stabilization Unit: Upon activation, stabilizes a critically injured character at 1 HP. Requires a Life Stabilization Check (DC 18). Restores consciousness for 1 minute, giving time for further treatment. Limited to one use per day per character. - Enhanced Life Preservation Device: Stabilizes a character at 5 HP and provides temporary resistance to death effects for 1 hour. Requires a Life Stabilization Check (DC 20). Failure renders the unit unusable until repaired with a Repair Check (DC 15). - Nano-Field Stabilizer: A miniaturized stabilizer that uses a focused nanobot swarm to halt bleeding and stabilize internal organs. Stabilizes a character at 1 HP, but with the added effect of slowly healing an additional 1d6 HP over the next 10 minutes. Limited to one use per character per day. - Defibrillator Gauntlets: Worn as gloves, these gauntlets deliver an electric shock to revive a character in critical condition. Requires a Medical Check (DC 15) to use effectively, stabilizing the target at 1 HP and restoring consciousness for 5 minutes. Misuse risks cardiac shock, causing 1d6 damage to the target instead. ---

Medical treatment includes physical care, surgery, or specialized methods tailored to the characterʼs species and injury type. - Basic First Aid: A Medicine Check (DC 10) restores 1d8 HP for minor wounds. Failed checks cause no healing but allow retries. First aid stops bleeding and stabilizes conditions. - Advanced Treatment: Medicine Check (DC 15) provides 2d8 HP healing, or 3d8 for severe injuries (DC 18). This includes techniques like bone-setting, wound closure, and bandaging. - Surgery and Trauma Care: Complex medical procedures can restore lost HP and reverse conditions (e.g., broken limbs, organ damage). Requires specialized tools and a Surgery Check (DC 18). Critical success restores HP fully, while failure risks further injury (-1 penalty to max HP). - Species-Specific Care: Characters of certain species (e.g., regenerating or elemental-based) benefit more from specific treatments. Medical kits tailored to a species grant a +2 bonus on recovery. ---

- Reduced Symptoms: A successful Meditation Check temporarily reduces the addiction level by one stage for 24 hours, allowing the character to function with fewer penalties. - Mental Fortification: Meditation grants a +1 bonus to Willpower Checks made against cravings and withdrawal symptoms for 24 hours. - Psychic Resilience: Characters who meditate successfully for seven consecutive days gain a permanent +1 bonus to Insight or Focus, as their mental resilience and clarity strengthen over time. - Stable Recovery: Meditation helps solidify long-term recovery. After completing 30 successful meditation days, the characterʼs Addiction Difficulty decreases by one permanent level, making cravings less frequent and severe.

- Frequency: Characters should meditate daily during the detox phase, gradually reducing frequency as they enter stabilization. - Willpower Meditation Check: Characters roll a Willpower Check against their Addiction Difficulty (AD) each day they meditate. Success grants specific benefits for that day and aids in long-term recovery.

Psionic healers skilled in mind restoration can heal mental and psychological trauma, stabilizing fractured minds or reviving a character who has fallen into a coma. - Calming Psionic Influence: By easing mental turmoil, the healer can relieve effects of fear, trauma, or mental ailments. A Psionic Check (DC 16) calms the target, removing any mental penalties for 1 hour. This effect can only be attempted on the same character once every 24 hours. - Mind Stitching: A technique used to help healers repair fragmented or damaged memories and reduce confusion or amnesia caused by trauma. The healer makes a Psionic Check (DC 18), restoring memory and clearing confusion, but may experience flashes of the targetʼs trauma. Each use requires a Resilience Check (DC 14) to avoid mental fatigue (imposing -1 to Insight for 8 hours). - Psychic Revival: For characters in a coma or unconscious due to psychic damage, the healer can attempt revival through intense psionic focus. A Psionic Willpower Check (DC 20) is required to reach the targetʼs mind and initiate revival. On success, the target regains consciousness with 1 HP but is weakened, suffering -1 to all ability scores for 24 hours. ---

This ability allows a psionic healer to reduce or eliminate pain by mentally blocking pain signals, helping characters manage wounds without suffering immediate penalties. - Effect: Using a Psionic Check (DC 12), the healer suppresses pain-based penalties, granting the target immunity to these penalties and a temporary +1 Focus for 1 hour.

These alchemical creations neutralize specific harmful effects rather than directly healing HP. - Venom Purge: Quickly neutralizes poisons in the bloodstream, granting immunity to the same poison type for 24 hours. This elixir requires a Crafting Check (DC 12) and a Resilience Check (DC 12) by the user to avoid aftereffects, such as weakness or dizziness. - Curse-Nullifying Draught: Temporarily nullifies the effects of curses, allowing the character 6 hours of relief. Requires a Crafting Check (DC 15) and optional Occultism Check to improve duration by an additional 6 hours. After the effects wear off, the curse temporarily doubles in potency, requiring a Willpower Check (DC 15) to avoid adverse effects. - Hexbane Elixir: An advanced alchemical concoction that clears minor hexes or dark influences. Grants a +2 bonus to Willpower Checks against mental or spiritual curses for 12 hours. Use within 24 hours risks hallucinations or nightmares, requiring a Resilience Check (DC 12) to manage. --- ---

records.proposedName: Psionic Healing Risks and Side Effects
records.summary: Psionic healing is potent but comes with potential drawbacks, especially when used repeatedly or in extreme circumstances. - Mental Fatigue: Repeated psionic healing within a 24-hour period risks psychic exhaustion. Each additional healing attempt after the first requires a Resilience Check (DC 15 + number of uses). Failure causes the healer to suffer -1 to Willpower or Focus for 24 hours. - Overextension: If a healer uses advanced techniques, such as limb regeneration or psychic revival, they risk overextending their abilities. After completing such a technique, the healer must roll a Psionic Check (DC 14); on failure, they fall into a fatigued state, unable to use psionic abilities for 4 hours. - Energy Rebound: When channeling large amounts of energy (e.g., in Energy Transfer or Life Stabilization), there is a chance of energy rebound. On a failed Resilience Check (DC 16), the healer

Soul alignment is a rare and potent form of healing in which the healer aligns the targetʼs soul with the ethereal plane, drawing on its calming, restorative energies. - Healing Effect: A successful Spiritual Check (DC 18) allows the healer to restore 5d8 HP to the target, soothing both body and mind. The target also gains a +2 bonus to Willpower and Resilience Checks against mental ailments for the next 48 hours. - Soul Resonance: For characters with severe mental trauma, the healer may deepen the alignment by increasing the DC to 20. On a success, the target clears one level of mental fatigue, trauma, or confusion. - Risk of Overalignment: If a character undergoes more than one Soul Alignment within a week, they risk becoming “overaligned” with the ethereal plane. The target must succeed on a Willpower Check (DC 16) or experience disorientation, suffering -1 to Insight and Focus for 24 hours. - Spiritual Echoes: Occasionally, the ritual leaves faint “echoes” from the ethereal plane. These echoes may linger for 48 hours, causing subtle auditory or visual phenomena around the target. Some creatures sensitive to ethereal energy may sense these echoes, potentially attracting curious or benign ethereal beings. ---

- Focused Visualization: By visualizing a specific goal, such as overcoming cravings or envisioning a future free of dependency, characters gain an additional +1 bonus on Willpower Checks made against cravings that day. - Grounding Techniques: In situations where cravings intensify, grounding exercises (e.g., breathing, visualization of protective energy) grant a +2 bonus on the next Willpower Check to avoid relapse. - Energy Channeling: Characters skilled in channeling energy (magical or psionic) may attempt to redirect cravings into productive energy, making a Focus Check (DC 12) to temporarily gain advantage on the next Willpower Check made against addiction.

These specialized items combine herbs and alchemy to address specific conditions or provide unique benefits. - Menderʼs Tonic: A warm, herb-infused drink that soothes pain and aids rest. Restores 1d6 HP and grants a +1 bonus to sleep-related recovery rolls for 8 hours. Consuming more than one dose in a day can cause sedation, imposing a -1 penalty to Alertness. - Essence of Vitality: This rare essence revives the userʼs energy and grants them 10 temporary HP for 12 hours. Also provides a +2 bonus to Strength for 4 hours, though the character suffers from fatigue once the effects wear off. - Mind-Clarity Brew: Removes confusion, mental fog, and grants a +2 bonus to Focus for 4 hours. May cause mild headaches if used multiple times in a day, requiring a Resilience Check (DC 10) to avoid penalty. - Stimulant Elixir: Sharpens the senses and heightens reaction times. Grants +1 bonus to Dexterity and Alertness for one hour but results in a -1 penalty to Willpower once the effect fades. - Nerve Rebuilder: A topical salve used for nerve damage, paralysis, or shock. Restores 1d4 HP per hour for 6 hours and grants a temporary bonus to Dexterity. Overuse risks overstimulation, causing trembling hands (-1 Dexterity for 24 hours). ---

This ritual allows the healer to communicate with a spiritual entity who grants healing in exchange for a service, insight, or energy. - Healing Effect: After a Spiritual Check (DC 18), the healer successfully communes with a benevolent spirit who bestows 3d10 HP healing to the target. - Insight of the Spirit: In return, the spirit may reveal hidden information, grant temporary Insight, or request a small service from the healer. - Overuse Consequence: Communing with spirits more than once per week risks draining the healerʼs energy, requiring a Resilience Check (DC 15). Failure results in a -1 penalty to Willpower for 48 hours due to spiritual fatigue.

Advanced technology allows for rapid healing, regeneration, and even body modification. - Nanobot Injection: Microbots injected into the bloodstream repair damaged tissue at the cellular level. Restores 2d8 HP immediately and another 2d8 over the next hour. Limited to one injection per day. - Regeneration Pods: Full-body pods accelerate healing by immersing the character in a regenerative solution while applying controlled electric pulses. A Bioengineering Check (DC 15) initiates regeneration, restoring 3d10 HP over eight hours. - Cybernetic Repair Modules: For characters with cybernetic or synthetic parts, these modules repair both organic and synthetic tissue. Restores lost HP to both biological and synthetic components, and reduces the risk of infection. Each use requires an Engineering Check (DC 12). - Life Stabilization Units: Portable, field-grade devices that prevent fatal injuries by stabilizing a characterʼs life force. On critical injuries, a Life Stabilization Check (DC 18) stabilizes HP at 1 and restores consciousness for one minute. ---
